newsitem.title: USA: US Senate leader hopes to cut capital gains taxes.
newsitem.headline: US Senate leader hopes to cut capital gains taxes.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Thursday he was hopeful Congress would cut capital gains and estate taxes this year, but did not think they would be abolished as he and many other Republicans want.

"I don't think we'll be able to eliminate them in one year," Lott, R-Mississippi, told reporters. He said he hoped there would be some reduction in the taxes as part of a budget reduction package. Lott also said he was concerned about administration proposals to increase some user fees and taxes and said Congress was not likely to approve them.
Lott said he and House Speaker Newt Gingrich expected to meet with President Clinton on the budget next week in a session originally planned for this week but delayed due to scheduling reasons.
